segments.oily: One reviewer with oily/combo skin reports the cream does not burn, break her out, strip, or dry her skin, while another with long-standing oily, acne-prone skin says it eventually cleared her skin and tamed oil.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin generally report hydration and no tightness or flaking, though a couple note the product dried their skin out and required layering extra moisturizer to compensate.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination or dry-combination skin describe it as gentle, non-irritating, and compatible with dry patches, calling it a good beginner option.
segments.sensitive: Most self-described sensitive-skin reviewers, including some with rosacea or eczema, report no irritation and successful gradual introduction, but a minority describe burns, rashes, or itchiness on sensitive skin, especially after a suspected formula change.
segments.mature: Reviewers who mention mature or aging skin (30s to 50s) report softened fine lines and improved texture over weeks to months, with one saying it minimizes fine lines without the dryness typical of aging skin.

concerns.aging: Multiple reviewers report visible softening of fine lines, wrinkles, and crow's feet with consistent use over weeks to months; one reviewer felt the low retinol percentage was too gentle to affect her fine lines.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers, including those with dry skin, report the cream is hydrating or non-drying and even helps with flaky, blotchy skin; others explicitly report it dried their skin out, especially at the start or during a formula change, requiring extra moisturizer.
concerns.redness: Reviewers with rosacea or reactive skin report calming effects and no added redness; however, some reviewers report new rashes, chemical burns, or worsened irritation, particularly linked to a suspected reformulation.
concerns.barrier: Some reviewers say the product helped restore or protect a damaged skin barrier compared to a harsher prescription retinol; a couple report the opposite, describing chemical burns or an allergic-type reaction they attribute to the product.
concerns.spots: Numerous reviewers report fading of dark spots, sun spots, and post-acne marks over weeks to months; no dissent on this concern was found.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers with acne-prone or hormonal-acne skin report reduced breakouts, faster healing of pimples, and clearer skin over time; a notable minority report new breakouts, cystic pimples, or worsening acne, some attributing it to comedogenic ingredients or a reformulation.
concerns.oiliness: A small number of reviewers with oily skin report the product tamed excess oil over time, with no reviewers reporting increased oiliness.

aspects.libelle: Tube packaging hard to fully empty

extraits.titre: New version is nothing like the old one
extraits.texte: I used this retinol cream for nearly a year (and swore by it) and it worked well for my skin—until recently, when i could swear GM quietly changed the formula and packaging. Not only does the new version smell HORRIBLE, but it caused me to have a severe breakout and what I believe was an allergic reaction. My skin has never reacted this badly to a skincare product before and I know for a fact it is directly linked to using this cream. It's really disappointing that such a reliable product was altered without any clear notice. The new tube looks different, the texture feels off, (and you can definitely tell by the smell) and unfortunately, the results are the complete opposite of what I experienced before. I won't be repurchasing, and I'd caution others who had success with the old formula to be very careful with this new one!!

I have mildly sensitive skin. I acclimated my skin to this by applying it on top of moisturizer for a week before i began applying it before moisturizer. A week after that, it gave me minor chemical burns. If your skin is at ALL sensitive, DON'T buy this.

I am 24 and have been struggling with painful acne on my jaw for the first time since my mid-teens. It has been about six months of active breakouts, where I wake up with a new pimple or cyst every single day, and the marks can't be covered by makeup. I added this to my nighttime skincare routine (every other day) a little over a week ago and I am pimple-free for the first time since summer. I have also recently started a skin supplement, so I do think the combination of those together is what's made the difference, but for $8 this is incredible. I am so happy with how quickly I saw results and how my face does not hurt anymore!! I will say this dried me out pretty bad as someone who already had dry skin, so I keep the rest of my routine pretty hydrating to even that out. But yes I love this it's definitely worth the buy for adult hormonal acne!!

extraits.titre: Perfect for beginners or sensitive skin
extraits.texte: I've tried a couple different times to incorporate retinols into my skincare routine but I have INCREDIBLY sensitive skin. Each time I tried my skin would break out into an irritated rash and become super damaged in just one or two uses. I saw this one claimed to be gentle and it was super affordable so I gave it a try and its worked great! I had to incorporate it very slowly over a few weeks into my skincare routine but now I can apply it almost nightly with no problems. And my skin definitely looks brighter and I've noticed some of my fine lines and scars have faded a bit after using it now for about 6 months. At such an affordable price point, this product is definitely worth a shot for people trying to use retinol for the first time or people with ultra sensitive skin like me.

I have sensitive skin prone to breaking out in a rash, but this was definitely gentle enough for my skin. I'm 35, pale, struggle with rosecea and some acne and have mild signs of aging and sun damage. I use this about 3-4 times a week with zero problems. I use a scentless basic hydrating moisturizer after and in the morning I use a salicylic acid and aloe gel and a rose infused moisturizer and havent had any issues. ther w were some minor breakouts at first, but ive read thats normal.

This was a great intro to retinoids to prep my skin for higher concentrations of retin and go from retinol to retinaldehyde with the least irritation possible. I used a tube of this over the course of about 6 months on my face, neck and chest. For about the first 2 months, I had very mild skin flaking and only applied a minimal amount on my skin every 3 days, then every other day, until I could apply it every day with no irritation. My skin became dramatically smoother, with improved texture and light wrinkles mostly disappeared. Retinoids require consistent use to see improvement so don't be discouraged if you don't see changes immediately; I only noticed a drastic change when I was several months in. This is a fantastic low price for a quality retin product and it is unfragranced. The cream is not oily, more like gel and never ran into my eyes. If it wasn't for the low percent of retinol, I'd happily still use it. Good Molecules, make a higher concentration with retinaldehyde for us!

I've been using the Good Molecules Gentle Retinol Cream for a little over a month now, and it has quickly become a staple in my nighttime routine. As someone with dry-combination skin, I've always been cautious about retinol because I worried it would make my dry areas worse—but this one is a total winner. The texture is creamy and moisturizing, and it doesn't leave my skin feeling tight or irritated. I apply it after cleansing and before my night cream, and I wake up with my skin feeling smooth, calm, and hydrated. No flaking, no redness—just a more even tone and subtle glow. It's super affordable, which is a huge plus, and it layers well with other products. My dry patches have stayed in check, and I've even noticed some fine lines softening a bit. I highly recommend this if you're looking to ease into retinol without irritating your skin. Will definitely repurchase!
